deviceConversionPath.texSyncCost: IPA 650 / 643 windows with more than 80 MiB of texSync: 0.22-1.08 ms of texSync wall time per allocated MiB; on this host the ETC2 path costs 237.3 ms per guest MiB and the BC path 10.2
deviceConversionPath.expectedDeviceEffect: the BC-path rows: deviceStream, coldScene bc 32 / bc 256, threadedScene bc

deviceStream.what: device-shaped texSync stream on the BC path (the path the IPA 650 / 643 device takes): real ThreadedRenderer, two paced 5 s windows of 3,000 synchronizations after more than 3 s idle; MiB per window comparable with the device's 118-146 MiB (2,598-4,375 calls); the device's render-thread lag is unknown, hence 64 / 256 / 1024 in flight

componentShares.what: bytes per variant and the change each sub-change adds (negative = fewer bytes): control -> +in-place transcode -> +4,096-byte spare floor -> +smallest-fit search (= candidate)

deviceStream cold window 256 in flight.note: median of three runs for control and candidate, one run otherwise

warmSceneBestCase.note: the same 156 sizes reloaded at once from a pool the cold round just filled: not the device pattern (a transition follows more than 3 s of steady play, so the pool is cold)

hostMsPerGuestMiB.note: cold scene, 32 in flight, host x86-64 (wall time of create + write + synchronize)

limitation: GPU-thread bytes of the real synchronization code on a host (x86-64 .NET 10 JIT, not NativeAOT on iOS) with a host-renderer double. The device-shaped stream is a model: its shapes, its 1-in-60 large fragmented textures and its uploads in flight are chosen from the device counters, not taken from Hogwarts Legacy; its control reaches the device's 118-146 MiB per window only in the cold window and only with 1024 uploads in flight, and its next window stays far below the device's sustained rate, so the device keeps missing the pool for reasons the model does not reproduce. GC counts, pauses and promoted bytes are the host's with the device's GC settings and gen0 budget; the device's GC effect is known only from a device run's core-performance windows. No iPhone run.
